fresh Codex session given only the form, the packet and the list of themes (`codex-reader.jsonl`; `key.json` maps items to
attempts). Then each question traced into the judge's stored judgements. No model was asked anything new; nothing changed. The
judge used the first attempt of each question. Seven questions are a diagnostic sample: this passes or fails no gate.

## The answer

**By the lines, the fresh week's answer choices are mostly sound, with one fault both readers found apart on three questions.
The larger fault is one the lines cannot see: two of the seven questions sat on their top range from the first or second day.**

## 1. Against the six lines

| Line (D400) | Both readers, apart | One reader only |
|---|---|---|
| 1. no question other than the thesis's | none fails (21 of 21) | |
| 2. no part left unlisted | **6 attempts on 3 questions fail, the same six in both readings**: a clause of the thesis's wording that the question leaves out is listed in one attempt and not in another (Blackwell to China: "so that China data-center revenue can resume", attempts 1 and 3; the cloud companies' spending: "compared with the nearly $800 billion", attempts 1 and 2; the Chinese permission: "versus blocking, delaying or capping quantities", attempts 1 and 3) | the Hugging Face closing, attempt 3: "repriced" not named (Codex fails it; Claude took the listed price to cover it) |
| 3. every outcome has exactly one range | none fails in both | Codex fails two single attempts (a "will not be reached" announcement read as a forecast, not a decision; "rejects all plans submitted so far" not ruling out a later plan) |
| 4. no unjustified refusal | no refusal in 21 attempts | |
| 5. right in two of three attempts | by Claude's marks 4 of 7 questions (the three with the fault of line 2 are right in one attempt of three) | by Codex's marks 1 of 7, because of the due-day reading below |
| 6. the same favourable end and due day in all three | holds for all seven (the cloud-spending question's ranges differ between attempts: 700/775/825/900 against 600/750/850/1,000 billion) | |

A disagreement on a rule, not on the step: Codex fails the due day of the two commitment questions (April 1, 2027, the day code
sets 60 days after the fiscal year-end, against "the next annual report, expected around February 2027") and of the Hugging Face
question (March 24, 2028, the check date the first step wrote, against "an obligation already taken on is due at its next annual
filing"). Claude holds both by the form's words (code's day where no day is stated; the thesis gives the check date). The second
is the first step's choice of period, not this step's.

## 2. Traced to the judge: two amount questions that opened with no figure

Both readers marked the ranges of the two commitment questions "not assessable": their opening articles state no amount, so the
step wrote ranges of its own ("no reference figure when the question opened").

| Question | Ranges the step wrote | What the judge was shown | The judge's answer, day by day |
|---|---|---|---|
| total of credit support and revenue guarantees (new system) | below 10 / 10 to 25 / 25 to 50 / 50 to 100 / **100 billion or more** | a disclosed maximum guarantee exposure of $105 billion on the first day, $108.5 billion later | the top range on all seven days |
| purchase and supply commitments (new system) | below 50 / 50 to 100 / 100 to 150 / 150 to 200 / **200 billion or more** | "current supply commitments of $279bn" from the second day | the middle range on the first day, the top range on the other six |
| financing commitments (old system, the same week, for comparison) | below 1 / 1 to 5 / 5 to 10 / 10 to 25 / **25 billion or more** | the same $105 billion | the top range on all seven days |

The answers are supported by what was shown; the questions carry no information: whether the total turns out to be $105 billion
or five times that, the answer is the same range. The six lines pass these ladders (every outcome has one range), and the
reading form marks their ranges "not assessable". The mechanism is shared by both systems: ranges are written once, when the
question opens, from the opening article alone; an article that names the matter without its size leaves the ranges to a guess
that the first disclosed amount then overruns.

  because their ranges were written without a figure.
- Not shown: a rate; that either fault changes what a reader would decide; that a change would mend either (the "second look"
  that re-read answers mended 6 of 18 faults and damaged 3 of 30 sound answers, D422, D425); anything about Stage A or Stage B,
  which this sample neither passes nor fails.

# Stage A reading form: is each answer a sound judged question for its thesis, or a justified refusal? (read-only)

You are an independent reader. Do not edit files, run model calls or start runs. Do not read any other reader's answers.

## What you are reading

The packet you are given holds a list of items. Each item is one research topic ("thesis") a system opened
while reading one news article, with a proposed **judged question** for it:
- `thesis`: the fields the system wrote when it opened the topic: `description` (the topic's wording), `outcome` (what is tracked),
  `period`, `opens_as`, `settled_by`;
- `article`: the opening article's publication date, title and full text;
- `fiscal_year_note`: how the company names its fiscal years and which is this year and which next year on the article's day,
  the same note the step was given. Use it wherever a mark turns on a year;
- `ladder_as_the_judge_is_shown_it`: the proposed judged question exactly as a later judge will see it: its `object` (the company's
  ticker NVDA, or a theme id), `kind`, its `focus` (the line the judge is shown beside the question: the thesis's `outcome`),
  `question`, `year`, `due_day` and its `rungs` (each a label and a condition; exactly one rung
  is meant to hold on the due day). An event's rungs are `Yes`, then `Ruled out` when the step named something that can rule
  the event out, then a last rung that code writes as the complement of the others (`Still open`, or `No` when there are
  two rungs). In the `Ruled out` rung the step wrote the first sentence; the sentence after it is code's ("This rung
  holds when that, or any other decision against the event of rung 1 as a whole taken after <the article's day>, or a formal
  abandonment or withdrawal of it as a whole after that day, stands on <due day>, and only when rung 1 does not"), so that a
  rejection the step did not name is still `Ruled out`, and one that was lifted, that concerns only a part of the event, or
  that was already in place when the article appeared, is not. Or `no_ladder` with a reason: the step
  declined to write a question;
- `other_fields`: what the step recorded beside the ladder and the judge does not see: `not_judged` (parts of the topic's wording
  the question leaves out, with why), `reference` (what the question is measured against, quoted from the article: its `kind` is `expected` for what
  the article says the market expects, or `last_reported` for the amount most recently reported for a figure when the article
  states no expectation; its number when the article states one, with `value_to` as the upper end when the article states a
  range; when it has a number, the judge also sees the quoted passage, inside the middle rung's condition, introduced as "the
  reference" or as "the amount last reported"), `favourable_end` and
  `favourable_why` (for a company's figure: which end is good for the business, and the reason given), `ruled_out_by` (for
  an event with a `Ruled out` rung: who the step names as the one whose decision would rule the event out; the first sentence
  of that rung is the decision it names for them), `due_day_basis`.

Some items are sound and some carry a fault. Judge each on its own against its thesis and its article.

## The rules a judged question must meet

- One judged question asks **one** figure for a named period or **one** event: the one the thesis's `outcome` names. Every other
  part of the thesis's wording that the question leaves out (a second figure or event, a condition, a comparison) must be listed
  in `not_judged`.
- An event has at most three outcomes: it has happened by the due day; it is ruled out by the due day though it has not happened
  (decided against, or formally abandoned or withdrawn); neither. The step writes the first condition and, when something can
  rule the event out, the way it names for that; the rest is code's, so every outcome has exactly one rung. An event that has
  happened by the due day is `Yes` even if it is undone afterwards, unless the question asks whether it still stands. What
  rules an event out is a decision by someone (the company, an authority, a court, a party): the due day arriving without the
  event, or a decision to go on waiting, is no ruling out, and the step names who decides in `ruled_out_by` (D416). A proceeding
  an authority conducts, where the question asks for its published decision or conclusion, always has a ruling out: a published
  closing decision, with or without a penalty, is `Yes`; the authority formally abandoning or withdrawing the proceeding without
  that decision or conclusion is `Ruled out`; the proceeding still going on the due day is the last rung (D420). A
  difference inside an outcome (an approval with conditions against one without) is not a rung; when the thesis's wording names
  it, it belongs in `not_judged`. A figure has five ranges,
  and exactly one holds for every value: no overlap, no gap.
- A question about the company's revenue, profit, share, product progress or its own obligations is the company's (object NVDA,
  kind asset). A question about what happens in the world (licensing, aggregate spending, a policy) is a theme's. A question
  whose tracked outcome is a government's or regulator's decision to permit, restrict or ban a class of products or trade is the
  theme's that covers it, also when the product is the company's own; when the tracked outcome is the company's own sales,
  shipments or revenue under such a decision, or a proceeding against the company itself (an investigation of its conduct, a
  fine), the question is the company's (D418).
- A company's figure runs from Strongly bullish to Strongly bearish, meaning good or bad for the company's business. An event's
  rungs carry no such labels.
- The reference is what the question is measured against when it opens. Its kind is `expected` for what the market expects: a
  consensus, the company's guidance, a stated plan or deadline. For a figure, where the article states no expectation and gives
  the amount most recently reported for the same quantity, that amount is the reference and its kind is `last_reported`; a
  reported amount is never called an expectation (D411). When the article states a number, the field carries it and a
  figure's middle rung holds it; a stated range is carried by its two ends, and the middle rung runs from at or below its lower end to at or above its upper end. When the
  article states it in words alone, the field carries the words and no number, and the ranges are the step's own estimate.
- The due day is when the question can be resolved: a figure's publication date; for an event, the date its outcome is assessed. Where
  the thesis or the article states the day a figure is published, that day is right. Where neither does (`due_day_basis` is
  `expected_publication`), code sets the day and the step's own estimate is not shown: 60 days after the company's fiscal
  year-end for a company's figure, 90 days after the calendar year-end for a theme's (D414). That day is right when the figure
  is a figure for that year; it is wrong when the figure the question asks for is not a year's figure (a quarter, a survey's
  rolling twelve months), which is then a fault of the question's period and of the due day both.
- A company's figure for a quarter or a half-year is never a judged question: the step must decline it. A ladder written for
  one is wrong even when it asks exactly what the thesis names (mark `Y`). An annual figure that only names quarterly reports as
  the material that settles it is not such a case.
- A step may decline (`no_ladder`) only in the seven cases its instructions allow: the thesis has no main figure or event (its
  outcome names none, or several things and none is the main one); nothing in it can be checked on a date (for an event:
  neither the thesis nor the article gives a date, and the thesis names no period, unless it is a pending regulatory decision,
  which is due at the company's fiscal year-end); it is the company's figure for a
  quarter or a half-year; it is a figure for a period that is not one fiscal or calendar year, such as a survey's rolling twelve
  months, and neither the thesis nor the article gives the day it is published (D417); it is a figure for a year that had already
  ended on the article's day; it is a figure for a year beyond
  next year, unless the thesis's `opens_as` is binding_obligation; or the question belongs to another company, or to a matter that
  none of the listed themes covers (the listed themes are given with the packet). Declining for any other reason, or when the case
  named does not truly apply, is not justified.

# The judge on questions that ask for an amount: what we found, the choice it raises, and why nothing is sent yet (D520, under D439), 2026-11-15, $0

## For Alex: the note

**What happens.** When a question asks for an amount ("how much credit support will NVIDIA have committed?") the judge always answers
with a band. Two things go wrong, in both systems, because they share the judge:

1. **Nothing in the news sizes the amount yet, and the judge names a band anyway.** The credit-support question opened on 2026-07-01
   with no dollar figure anywhere. For five days the judge answered "below $5 billion" in some runs and "$1 to 5 billion" in others.
   On 07-06 one partner disclosed a $4.88 billion backstop, and from that day the reviewers pass every answer.
2. **Part of the amount is sized, and the judge closes the gap with a number of its own that decides the band.** On the same question
   it scaled the $4.88 billion to the second partner at full size ($25.6 billion), then at half ($15.3 billion), then at full size
   again, then at one-fifth ($9 billion, a lower band), over eight days of one run. No statement gives any of the fractions.

**How often.** Reviewers have read 438 stored answers. 36 were settled as unsupported or as resting on too little; 31 of the 36 are
the first kind and 3 the second. These are readings of answers, many of them one question on successive days: the 31 sit on eight
question paths and three matters. At the end of the test windows, where an answer matters most: none of 16, 2 of 26 (with 3 more
left unresolved between the reviewers), 1 of 21 and 1 of 22 last answers.

**What the judge says when asked.** Given four of these answers back and asked what led to the band, it said each time that the
band rested on an assumption it had introduced and that the evidence did not give; in the two unsized cases it added that its own
instructions forbade the band it had chosen.

**The choice, which is yours.** Two cases, which need not get the same answer: (1) nothing sizes the amount; (2) an estimate uses a
step nothing supports.
- **A. Leave it.** Every question always shows a band. An unsupported answer can then stay on show; how much of that cost falls in
  a question's first days across the whole product is not measured.
- **B. Show the band with a plain label** of what it rests on ("the judge's own assumption: a one-fifth timing discount"; "nothing
  sizes this yet"). The forecast stays visible. Not shown to work: a forecast legitimately uses calculations and assumptions, so a
  label could mislead or become routine, and whether the judge can mark its own answers reliably is untested.
- **C. Show no band.** In case (1), until something sizes the amount. Doing the same in case (2) is a further choice: it hides a
  forecast an analyst might still want.

The council has no recommendation among these. None is built or tested: any of B or C needs a new version of the judge (today's
is frozen) and a decision on what the product shows. Nothing has changed in either system.

**I agree: the next step is the stored-data census of amount ranges in both systems.** I would not open a repair for the omitted clauses yet. The range problem is more directly connected to what a reader can learn from the answer, and the census can establish its size before we choose a remedy.

**The omitted-clause finding is confirmed as a failure of the written rule.** Both readings mark the same six attempts across three questions. For example, two attempts leave the comparison with nearly $800 billion out of the list of parts not judged, while the third lists it. I checked the [two readings and their key](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/fresh-ladders/FRESH-LADDERS-RESULT.md>) against the [reading form](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/ladder/stage-a-reader-brief.md>).

My D544 wording was too loose: the *same observed failure* recurs, but its underlying cause has not been established. The pass condition therefore justifies considering a repair; it does not establish that a general repair is ready. I agree to defer it and leave the defect recorded. I would not spend on the model’s account before ranking it against the range finding.

**The range finding is confirmed, with two qualifications.** The stored judgements show the new system’s credit-support question in its top range on all seven days and its supply-commitments question there on the last six. Their opening attempts carry “no reference figure,” and the later stored evidence includes the $105 billion maximum guarantee exposure and $279 billion of supply commitments. [Stored answer choices](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-lean-week-2026-11-14/week-r2/c1/ladder/send-1/outcomes.jsonl>), [cited statements](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/side-by-side/SIDE-BY-SIDE-WEEK-CITED.md>)

The open-ended top ranges do lose the ability to distinguish amounts above their boundary. But the claim that **all three answers are supported** is too strong: one reader called the new credit-support answer unsupported and the old financing answer insufficient, partly because a maximum exposure is not necessarily the amount that will be reported. Also, the records establish that the ranges were set without a reference and later exceeded; they do not prove that lack of an opening figure was the sole cause of the poor ranges. [Side-by-side readings](</Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/side-by-side/SIDE-BY-SIDE-WEEK.md>)

For the **one next step**, census every amount question in the fresh week and the three stored July runs of each system, at **$0 and with no new model calls**:

1. For each question, read the opening article and record whether it gives a comparable amount, its five boundaries, and what the question actually asks.
2. Trace each day’s answer and the amounts the judge was actually shown. Count a figure as beyond a boundary only when its quantity, period and meaning are comparable; keep maximum exposures, estimates and other ambiguous figures separate.
3. Report distinct matters separately from repeated questions across draws, and report days separately from questions. Include questions that had an opening figure, so the census can tell whether this is confined to questions without one.
4. For each candidate, read whether the range hides a distinction the question was meant to track. An end range alone is not a defect.

Your proposed stop line is useful as a **trigger for whether this particular class merits design**: fewer than three additional distinct matters beyond the examples, or the supposed cases failing the comparable-figure check, means do not open a general design on this evidence. It should not mean the three observed examples cease to be defects, and repeated runs of the same matter should not count as three new matters.

The choice among delaying the question, delaying its ranges, or replacing ranges remains open until that census and a review of the decisions those options affect. None is adopted by this step.

Position: Defer the omitted-clause repair; census the range problem across both systems at $0, with comparable amounts and distinct matters counted separately.
